key_insight: Bi-FORK tackles bifurcation problems where one input can lead to multiple valid outcomes, instead of forcing a single prediction. It learns the full set of possible trajectories in high-dimensional systems, capturing symmetry-breaking behavior that standard surrogates miss.
problem_solved: Most deep learning surrogates assume a one-to-one mapping from input to output, which fails for bifurcating systems with multiple equally valid solutions. This paper addresses the challenge of modeling one-to-many solution maps in complex physical dynamics.
method: Introduces Bi-FORK, a generative framework designed specifically for high-dimensional bifurcating systems.
Produces complete trajectories rather than a single deterministic output, representing multiple valid branches of the solution space.
Learns the structure of symmetry-breaking bifurcations so the model can generate diverse physically plausible outcomes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this opens the door to more realistic surrogate modeling for systems with intrinsic ambiguity and branching behavior. It is especially relevant for scientific ML in physics, engineering, climate, and other domains where multiple outcomes can arise from the same conditions.
visual_elements: A branching trajectory diagram showing one input splitting into multiple valid solution paths

paper_title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
paper_authors: Anna Zimmel, Fleur Hendriks, Markus Holzleitner, Florian Sestak, Martin Weichselbaumer
